title: What Are Landing Pages, Ecommerce Stores and Portfolio Websites?
content:
As you begin your frontend training, you will be building three types of websites. 

Before we dive in, here is a quick breakdown of what each one means and what you will be able to do with your skills as you grow.

## Landing Page 

https://res.cloudinary.com/di4dlnd5x/image/upload/v1782654601/Sign-up-landing-page-cover-9_v5jouq.webp

A landing page is a single focused webpage designed to get visitors to take one specific action, such as signing up, downloading something or clicking a button. It has no distractions, just one goal. 

In Nigeria, companies like Paystack, Flutterwave and PiggyVest use powerful landing pages to convert visitors into users. Every time you saw a "Get Started" or "Join the Waitlist" page from a Nigerian startup, that was a landing page doing its job.

## Ecommerce Store

https://res.cloudinary.com/di4dlnd5x/image/upload/v1782653382/Ecommerce-Website-Development_l4upk3.png

An ecommerce store is a website where products or services are sold online. 

Think of it like a physical shop but on the internet. Jumia, Konga and Jiji are the most recognisable examples in Nigeria. Even smaller Nigerian businesses like fashion vendors and food brands now run their own online stores to reach customers across the country.

## Portfolio Website

https://res.cloudinary.com/di4dlnd5x/image/upload/v1782653369/0_6GW0JRSClQd23ZqU_qz00tt.jpg

A portfolio website is your personal showcase. 

It displays your work, skills and experience so potential clients or employers can find you and decide to hire you. 

Many Nigerian developers and designers who now work remotely for international companies started by building a simple portfolio website. It is often the first thing a client asks for before they hire you.

## What You Can Build With Frontend Skills Alone (Free Course)

https://res.cloudinary.com/di4dlnd5x/image/upload/v1782663947/frontend_nm4j9p.png

With just the frontend, you can build websites that look great and work smoothly in a browser. These include:

A landing page to promote a product, event or service
A personal or professional portfolio to showcase your work
A static ecommerce store layout where products are displayed
A business or brand website for a client
A restaurant, church or NGO website
A personal blog layout

These are fully functional, real websites you can show to clients and get paid for.
Who Is Looking for These Skills Around You
You do not need to look far for your first client. The people who need what you are learning are already around you:

The fashion vendor selling on WhatsApp status who has no real website and loses customers the moment her phone is off
The small restaurant or bukka owner who wants people to find their menu and location online
The private school that is still using a WhatsApp group to communicate with parents instead of a proper website
The hair salon, barbing shop or spa that has no online presence and relies only on word of mouth
The event planner who creates a new flyer for every event but has nowhere permanent online to send people
The church or mosque that wants to share sermons, announce programmes and reach new members online
The photographer or makeup artist whose only portfolio is an Instagram page they cannot control

These are real people in your street, your estate and your community. They need you and most of them do not even know it yet.

## What You Can Build When You Add Backend Skills (Paid Course)

https://res.cloudinary.com/di4dlnd5x/image/upload/v1782663955/1640269661861_xtedse.png

The paid course unlocks the engine behind the websites. When you combine frontend with backend, domain, hosting and monetization strategy, you can build:

A fully working ecommerce store where the fashion vendor's customers can browse, add to cart and pay without needing to send a DM
A school website where the admin can log in and update notices, results and fees without calling a developer
A restaurant website where the menu updates live and customers can place orders directly
A booking system for salons, spas and event planners where clients can schedule appointments online
A church website where new sermons and announcements are published from a simple dashboard
A personal portfolio with a working contact form that sends messages straight to your email

This is where your skill stops being something you learned and becomes something that pays you consistently.

## Where Nigerians Are Already Earning a Living With These Skills

https://res.cloudinary.com/di4dlnd5x/image/upload/v1782663935/Untitled-design-1024x576_wn3thk.webp

Over 4 million Nigerians are currently active on freelancing platforms, making it one of the fastest growing freelancer populations in Africa. Here is where they are earning:

Upwork where skilled Nigerian developers earn between $15 and $80 per hour with top earners pulling in over $5,000 monthly
Fiverr where website projects sell from $50 to $2,000 and many Nigerians have built full time income from it
Toptal which connects elite developers to companies paying premium rates, with some Nigerian developers earning above $10,000 monthly
LinkedIn which has become a major platform where Nigerian developers land remote jobs paying in dollars
Freelancer.com where Nigerians compete for web design and development projects daily

The opportunity is real, the market is wide open and the skills you are learning this week are the foundation for all of it.
